answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by growing trust like an orchard: slowly, through seasons of real work. A new identity starts with a tiny transaction ceiling and must earn signed attestations from independent counterparties for completed jobs, each a quill stroke on a public ledger. Raising the ceiling takes months of vouched work plus a refundable stake, slashed on fraud. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities meets only a zephyr of empty promises: no history, no attestations, no stake, a ceiling too low to matter. Faking that history costs more than fraud could repay.
